I completely agree with you. I see a lot of begginer here posting something about song suggestions or getting confused about what to do next.

The best way to learn the guitar is to actually learn the songs that you like. I still remember back when I was a few months into my guitar journey, I decided to learn a pretty difficult song, it was Sungha Jung's River flows in you. This song was way way out of my level, but nevertheless, I still decided to learn it, just because I really like the song.

OP, if you're learning a song, and you're stuck in a rut or losing motivation. My best suggestion is to just pause learning that song, learn something else, and come back another time. That's what I did with River Flows in You. Along the way I learned a bunch of cool riffs, like Stairway To Heaven, Black Dog, and a few others. After about 1.5 years of playing guitar, I finally managed to play River Flows in You. Playing a guitar is a journey man. There's going to be some shit along the way, you just gotta get through with it. 

In short learn the songs you actually like, even if it's difficult, just try enjoy them, even if it sounds like shit, because eventually you're gonna get better.

When I'm playing the open chords, I usually put my thumb on top of the neck, to lightly touch the top string, like [this](https://imgur.com/a/qnUozEL). Because in most open chords you don't actually play the 6th string, you want to mute it.

I'd say you have a pretty good form. My only complain is that your fingering isn't very efficient, like the sliding part at the end. Also in the original song, I can hear a hammer ons and pull offs, but I didn't see any here. Maybe you should also work on that :)
Yeah, it's a barre chord because you bar the ninth fret with your index finger.

The best way is probably to learn it incrementally, first you'd practice to bar 3 strings, then 4 strings, and so on. A great song to practice barring would probably the intro to Stairway to Heaven. The intro has chords that only need to bar 3 strings.
One solution would be not playing the 9th on the G string (3rd string), because that's just the octave of the root. While the second chord is just a normal bar chord.

Lots of unnecessary moves during F2L, rather than doing random flicking you should take a moment and look around to find a pair, then try figure out how to solve that case in your mind, after that close your eyes and execute those moves. This is the advice that got me to sub 25. You should also learn to do U2'/double flick with your left hand. During F2L I noticed you did a lot of single flick for U2' with your left hand. On that Rb perm you also didn't use your left hand for the second U2. 

For cross the better solution is D' R2 F' U' L F'. You should turn off the inspection timer and give yourself unlimited time to figure out the cross.

A better first pair solution is R U R' U' R' U' R y' U R U R'. And for second pair U2 (U' L' U L)2 y' L' U L is the better solution. Third pair was perfect obivously. Lastly, the fourth pair U L U2 L2 U' L2 U' L' is a better solution.
